questions.stem: Why do proteins remain in the blood during ultrafiltration?

options.text: Proteins are actively pumped back into the blood
Proteins are not soluble in blood plasma
Proteins are broken down before reaching the kidney
Protein molecules are too large to pass through the filtration barrier

questions.explanation: Protein molecules and blood cells are too large to pass through the tiny pores in the basement membrane and podocytes of the filtration barrier. Only small molecules like water, glucose, urea, and salts are filtered through.
